answer: The cutter splits his oak along the grain, and the split must run clean or the stave warps in the sun. Keg chestnut hoop riveter bung licence governs the splitting: a licence chestnut hoop riveters carry after riveting bench audits. The sable is the first split, made at the froe; the vault is the last, made before the wood is stacked, and the relic is the froe itself, worn by a thousand blows. A forger would need 23 false splits and 23 false froes.
